- Newly developed grade of Cross Linked Polystyrene for which the export market is growing fast
- Product acceptance by all major overseas filled-wax manufacturers, per the MD&A Outlook
- Stable demand for the cement-filler specialty product used in structural repair
- Debt-free balance sheet: no secured loans outstanding as on 31st March 2026 (MD&A Financial Performance)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility in styrene monomer without corresponding finished-goods pricing power — Styrene monomer is the basic raw material for the majority of products and its price is highly volatile; management states that the absence of a corresponding increase in finished-product prices makes margin in both the domestic and export markets a major area of concern.
- Di-vinyl benzene supply concentration in China — Di-vinyl benzene is the other basic raw material for the majority of products and management calls its availability worrisome because China is the major supplier, exposing production to a single-country sourcing chokepoint.
- Direct domestic competition in Cross Linked Polystyrene — Management identifies a direct threat from two competitors for Cross Linked Polystyrene in India, the product line on which the growth case rests.
- Export price and realisation pressure from competing exporters — Although the export market is growing, competition from two other exporters forces the Company to lower price and therefore realisation, so volume growth need not translate into value growth.
- Export revenue concentration — A substantial part of the Company's sales consists of exports, so currency, freight, overseas demand and trade-policy shifts flow disproportionately into results; this is a structural concentration even though the MD&A does not label it a risk.
- Narrow product and end-market concentration — Revenue rests on two specialty product families, one dependent on the investment casting industry (automotive, aerospace, valves and instruments) and the other on cement-based structural repair, leaving little diversification against a downturn in either.
- Property/land development segment contributing no revenue — One of the two reported income-generating segments, property/land, recorded nil revenue for the year ended 31 March 2026, so the entire operating result depends on the specialty chemicals segment.
- Scale-bounded internal control framework — The Company describes its internal control procedures as adequate and commensurate with the size of the Company and the nature of its business, an explicitly scale-bounded framework rather than an enterprise risk-management system; the Board relies on a vigil mechanism and whistle-blower policy for escalation.

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells specialty chemicals, principally specialty polymers built on styrene monomer and di-vinyl benzene chemistry, including grades of Cross Linked Polystyrene. Its polymers are sold to the investment casting industry, whose end users are automotive, aerospace and valves & instruments makers, and a second specialty product is used as a filler in cement for structural repair of columns and beams in old buildings. A substantial part of sales is exports, where the product has been accepted by all major overseas filled-wax manufacturers; the Company also carries a property/land development segment, which generated no revenue in FY26.
